business_problem: Anxin Insurance needed to launch quickly under strict financial-regulatory constraints, avoid building a physical data center, migrate legacy finance workloads safely, and use data to improve product innovation and anti-fraud controls.
solution_summary: Anxin Insurance used Tencent Cloud to launch as a fully internet-native insurer without first building a traditional on-premises financial data center. All business systems were deployed in Tencent Cloud's financial-grade environment, which helped the company meet tight opening timelines while satisfying strict regulatory facility requirements. Tencent also supported seamless Oracle migration so legacy finance workloads could move to the cloud without a costly rewrite, and paired the infrastructure with big-data analytics for customer-needs analysis, product innovation, and anti-fraud controls. COS-backed video and image uploads from mobile devices feed underwriting assistance, while social channels and mobile payments help connect customer service, onboarding, and claims experiences. The architecture gave Anxin an elastic, lower-cost base for insurance operations while using data and security controls to improve product design, risk management, and digital customer experience.

solution_components.role: Uses data-driven controls to strengthen risk identification and anti-insurance-fraud operations.

solution_components.name: WeChat & QQ Payment Integration

data_flow: Core insurance systems run inside the financial data center, customer and business data feed the analytics and anti-fraud layers, mobile-uploaded video and image evidence are stored in COS for underwriting assistance, and payment and service interactions flow through WeChat and QQ-connected customer channels.
business_outcome: Tencent Cloud helped Anxin launch on time, lower infrastructure cost, pass financial-regulatory review, improve product innovation, and add scalable anti-fraud and customer-service capabilities to an internet-insurance model.
metrics: It became the first domestic insurer to pass regulatory acceptance with all systems running in the cloud.
